methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $20M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Kraftblock is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Martin Schichtel and Susanne König, having raised €20M+ to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private—spanning frontier energy and materials, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $20M raised proxy, yielding $38M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C)—produces a median of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The wide peer range reflects heterogeneity in capital intensity and market opportunity within the climate tech subsector.

Triangulating these two methods yields a valuation range of $32M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $519M. The substantial gap between the stage-progression floor and peer-median estimate reflects Kraftblock's early stage relative to later-round Series C comparables. Key uncertainties include technology maturation pathway, capital requirements to commercialization, and whether peer valuations reflect sustainable market multiples or sector-specific froth. Additional due diligence on unit economics and go-to-market readiness would be necessary to narrow this range.
